Once I reached blood levels of 2.5 mmol (a measurement based on using the
Precision Xtra device), my pain effectively disappeared. Ketones have potent
anti-inflammatory effects. I am now testing using [The Slow-Carb
Diet](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wpm&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=z&)
instead, but supplementing with KetoForce exogenous ketones. So far, this
seems to be about three-quarters as effective (of course, I’m just an N of 1).

bullets.title: The Man Who Knew Infinity
bullets.note:
In 1913, Srinivasa Ramanujan, a self-taught Indian genius, traveled to
Cambridge where he forged a lifelong bond with his eccentric math professor,
G.H. Hardy, while fighting a world that refused to acknowledge his
achievements.  
  
It can be soul-crushing to be the “one (or two) against the many,” and this
movie reminded me of my wide-ranging conversation with Eric Weinstein, PhD
(“[Eric Weinstein on Challenging ‘Reality,’ Working with Peter Thiel, and
Destroying Education to Save
It](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wpa&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=9&)”).

bullets.title: The Daily Stoic
bullets.creator: now, most of you know how much I enjoy and recommend Stoic philosophies as an operating system, or a
bullets.note:
an operating system, or a set of principles for making better decisions. [This
book](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wpP&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=n&)
offers daily Stoic insights and exercises, featuring all-new translations from
the Emperor Marcus Aurelius, the playwright Seneca (my usual fave), and slave-
turned-philosopher Epictetus, in addition to lesser-known luminaries like
Zeno, Cleanthes, and Musonius Rufus. If you like the sound of a daily one-page
dose of Stoicism, here are two options:
[hardcover](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wpP&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=n&)
or audiobook on
[Audible](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wpi&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=j&).
